properties.displayName: Allowed locations
properties.description: This policy enables you to restrict the locations your organization can specify when deploying resources. Use to enforce your geo-compliance requirements. Excludes resource groups, Microsoft.AzureActiveDirectory/b2cDirectories, and resources that use the 'global' region.

properties.displayName: Not allowed resource types
properties.description: Restrict which resource types can be deployed in your environment. Limiting resource types can reduce the complexity and attack surface of your environment while also helping to manage costs. Compliance results are only shown for non-compliant resources.

properties.displayName: Secure transfer to storage accounts should be enabled
properties.description: Audits Storage accounts unless secure-transfer configuration is explicitly enabled. No request API-version gate is used. Missing configuration is reported rather than inferring compliance from an API-version-dependent service default.

metadata.description: Start in audit mode. Only effects supported by the source definition are available.

properties.displayName: Storage accounts should have the specified minimum TLS version
properties.description: Configure a minimum TLS version for secure communication between the client application and the storage account. To minimize security risk, the recommended minimum TLS version is the latest released version, which is currently TLS 1.2.

metadata.description: Start in audit mode. Only effects supported by the source definition are available.
Minimum version of TLS required to access data in this storage account

properties.displayName: Storage account public access should allow trusted services
properties.description: Audits storage accounts whose network rules do not allow Azure services on the trusted services list to access the storage account (the AzureServices network-rule exception).

metadata.description: Start in audit mode. Only effects supported by the source definition are available.

properties.displayName: Key vaults should have soft delete enabled
properties.description: Deleting a key vault without soft delete enabled permanently deletes all secrets, keys, and certificates stored in the key vault. Accidental deletion of a key vault can lead to permanent data loss. Soft delete allows you to recover an accidentally deleted key vault for a configurable retention period.

metadata.description: Start in audit mode. Only effects supported by the source definition are available.

properties.displayName: Key vaults should have deletion protection enabled
properties.description: Audits Key Vaults unless purge protection is explicitly enabled, excluding recovery operations. This is a property-based check without request API-version gates. Soft-delete configuration is covered by the separate Global soft-delete policy.

metadata.description: Start in audit mode. Only effects supported by the source definition are available.
